finding.observed: The repaired store correctly requires an existing fingerprinted SQLite file and binds real path plus device/inode. It also stores fingerprint.receipt_sha256() in each checkpoint row and load_generation requires the stored receipt to equal the store's current authority_receipt_sha256.
finding.why_unstable: UnifiedDBFingerprint.receipt_sha256 covers mutable observations including size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, whole-file sha256, sqlite schema digest/version/page count and sidecar flags. A legitimate WP-206 write can change these fields while the canonical database file remains the same dev/inode authority. A fresh process that fingerprints the same post-write file will therefore obtain a different full receipt hash and can reject an otherwise valid persisted checkpoint solely because the database mutated as intended.
finding.required_model: Separate stable file ownership identity from point-in-time fingerprint provenance. Stable identity should bind at least canonical real_path + device + inode (or an admitted equivalent stable authority token). Each write receipt may additionally preserve the full point-in-time UnifiedDBFingerprint receipt. Row validation across restart should compare the stable file identity and preserve the historical full receipt as provenance; it must not require current mutable fingerprint receipt equality after authorized mutation. File replacement (device/inode change) remains fail-closed.

required_tests: Create an existing SQLite UnifiedDB, fingerprint it, open WP-206 store, persist generation 0, close process.
Fresh process re-fingerprints the same mutated DB and must load generation 0 successfully because real_path/device/inode remain the same even though full fingerprint receipt changes.
Fresh process persists generation 1 with its new point-in-time fingerprint provenance and parent digest bound to generation 0.
A later fresh process re-fingerprints and loads generation 1 successfully.
Replacing the DB file at the same path must still fail because device/inode identity changes.
Historical write-receipt fingerprint hashes remain preserved as provenance and are never rewritten to the newest fingerprint.
next_exact_action: Replace current-row equality against mutable full fingerprint receipt with a stable canonical-file identity binding plus historical per-write fingerprint provenance. Update subprocess tests to create an explicit existing SQLite fixture, pass resolution + fresh fingerprint in every process, use current caller: adoption syntax, and prove restart across post-write re-fingerprinting before hosted CI can be accepted.
